en: Therīgāthā 5.2 Pañcakanipāta: The Verses of the Elder Nun Vimalā I have crossed over the flood; I am free from fear. Having abandoned all attachments, I dwell at peace. My mind is well-liberated through right knowledge; I have attained the state that is truly secure. I was once a courtesan, skilled in the arts of love; I was beautiful, youthful, and endowed with charm. But having seen the Blessed One, the peerless Buddha, I renounced the world and entered homelessness. For many years I have practiced the holy life Under the guidance of the Teacher, the Great Sage. Having cut off the stream of rebirth, I have reached the end of suffering. I am now one who has done her duty; I am a nun who has lived the life. With the destruction of all taints, I have realized for myself the state of peace. I pay homage to the Teacher, the Great Sage, Who has shown me the path to liberation.

Through his teaching, I have crossed over the ocean of existence; I have reached the further shore, free from all fear. I am now one who has transcended birth and death; I am one who has put an end to suffering. I am a nun who has attained the goal; I am one who has realized the Dhamma. “Exceedingly endowed with beauty, form,
charm, and glory,
And arrogant because of her youth;”
I did not despise others.
Having adorned this body,
which is beautifully decorated yet deceives the foolish;
I stood at the door of the brothel like a hunter who has set a snare,
displaying my ornaments.
I displayed many secrets and public displays;
I practiced various deceptions,
laughing loudly at many people.
Having wandered for alms today,
shaven-headed and clad in the outer robe,
she sat at the foot of a tree.
She has attained the state free from applied thought.
All bonds have been severed—
those that are divine and those that are human.
“Having expelled all taints,
I have become cooled and attained nibbāna.
… Thus spoke the elder nun Vimalā, formerly a courtesan.
